post.caption: A royal crown's jewels were once rented. It is St Edward's Crown, made in 1661 for King Charles II, and it replaced a medieval crown that was melted down in 1649. The crown weighs nearly five pounds, and its hundreds of stones include amethysts and topazes. George V had the stones set permanently in 1911. It is used only for the moment of crowning. After that, the monarch switches to the Imperial State Crown, which is only about half as heavy. Charles III was crowned with it in 2023, and before then its band was adjusted to fit King Charles.
